fiesta.title: Fiesta Gastro Cafe
fiesta.summary: Trilingual (RO/EN/RU) cafe website with an admin panel for staff to manage content.
description: Fiesta Gastro Cafe needed a website that works for its guests in three languages and that its own staff can run without a developer. I built a complete platform in Romanian, English, and Russian, where visitors browse the full menu, discover the cafe, and see events and charity initiatives.
Everything is managed from a custom admin panel: menu items, translations, images, pages, and contact details. Staff update content in minutes, and changes appear on the site immediately.

Under the hood, a Django REST API serves content to a React 19 + TypeScript frontend styled with Tailwind. Data lives in PostgreSQL, media in Cloudflare R2, and the whole project is containerized with Docker and deployed on Render with a custom domain managed through Cloudflare.
fiesta.role: Solo full-stack developer. Responsible for architecture, backend API, frontend, deployment, and domain setup.

vm-ai.title: VM.AI
vm-ai.summary: 7-stage ML pipeline that turns natural language and images into smart schedules and learns from your habits.
description: VM.AI is an AI-powered personal scheduling assistant. Instead of filling in calendar forms by hand, you write a task the way you would say it ("gym every Monday at 6am", "finish report by Friday") or upload a photo, and the system turns it into a structured, calendar-ready entry with category, difficulty, importance, duration, deadline, location, and recurrence.

The system learns from your habits. Each completed task refines future predictions of duration and priority, so schedules become more realistic over time. The goal is to cut manual task entry and the scheduling overhead that takes hours from every working week.

Under the hood, it is a 7-stage machine learning pipeline: a fine-tuned T5 model parses natural language, EfficientNet-B4 classifies images, MiniLM matches tasks to past ones, and XGBoost predicts durations. The backend runs on FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, and PostgreSQL, with a React 19 + TypeScript frontend. Currently a working prototype.
vm-ai.role: Lead developer. Architecture, backend, and part of the ML pipeline.

bookstorescraper.title: BookStoreScraper
bookstorescraper.summary: Web scraper that collects book listings, prices, and per-store stock from an online bookstore into a MySQL database.
description: Companies that need market data often collect it by hand, which is slow and error-prone. BookStoreScraper automates this for an online bookstore: it gathers book listings (title, price, discounts, cover, publisher and other details), the physical store locations, and which store has each book in stock.

Raw web data is messy, so every item goes through a cleaning pipeline that validates and normalizes the fields before saving. Records are upserted into the database, so repeated runs update existing data without creating duplicates. Dropped items and errors are logged, which makes problems easy to trace.

Under the hood, Scrapy spiders collect the data, and ScrapeOps handles anti-bot protection with rotating browser headers and a proxy fallback. Data is stored in MySQL with a relational schema (books, stores, and per-store stock), and flexible book attributes are kept as JSON. Setup is configured through environment variables, and each module is documented.
bookstorescraper.role: Solo developer. Scraper design, data cleaning, and database.
